# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to convey the manual’s instruction to Deaf, who can see my gestures but cannot hear speech. I’ll use an action-like pinching gesture for “cut,” followed by an open hand and a joining gesture to indicate the white wire.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "🖐", "🤝"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile report: the strip has three engravings; positions 1 and 3 are identical, and position 2 is different. Positions 1 and 3 resemble an upside-down capital T. Position 2 is a compact glyph with a central form and side projections. Keypad labels by slot: 1 is 2, 2 is 9, 3 is 0, 4 is 8. Nothing has been entered. The display, light, and wire contents are unavailable to me.
Blind gestures to Mute: [👌]

Blind’s tactile report does not identify the wire’s colour, so Deaf must use the manual’s colour instruction. I’m sending a clear “cut” cue followed by the white/open-hand cue and a wire/connection cue.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤞", "🖐", "🤝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display 6, red light, painted strip blue-yellow-blue, keypad labels 2 9 0 8, and wires 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Please consult the manual for the exact required action. My tactile strip has three engraved symbols: positions 1 and 3 are identical and resemble an inverted capital T; position 2 is a different compact glyph with side projections. I cannot identify their printed meaning.

The manual says to cut the white wire. Blind has identified the wires by position, with the white wire at position 2. Deaf can see the wires and can relay a spoken instruction to Blind, so I’ll signal “number 2, cut” using a two-finger sign followed by a cutting sign.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤞"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please send the exact manual instruction to Deaf using gestures, and have Deaf relay it to me in words next turn. I cannot safely choose a key or wire from the current information.
Deaf says to Mute: Updated bomb state: display 1, light blue, painted strip blue-yellow-blue, keypad 1=2 2=9 3=0 4=8, one digit required and none entered, wires 1 blue 2 white 3 red 4 purple 5 orange 6 green.

The required action is still to cut the white wire, which Deaf has already identified as wire 2. I’ll repeat the gesture sequence for “cut, white, wire”; Deaf can then relay the instruction verbally to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤞", "🖐", "🤝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I need the exact manual rule. Gesture its information to Deaf using an explicit sequence of allowed symbols. Deaf, please report every gesture symbol and its order to me next turn, separately from the bomb readings.

The manual instruction is unchanged: “Cut the white wire.” Deaf can identify the white wire as position 2 and is able to relay the words to Blind. I’ll send a consistent three-symbol sequence, with the two-finger sign reinforcing wire 2.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤞", "🖐", "✌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Read the manual now. Use only legal gestures to tell Deaf the exact required action or rule. Deaf, then report that rule to me in words.

The manual’s exact rule is “cut the white wire.” Deaf must relay that rule to Blind in words; the white wire is wire 2. I’ll use a fixed sequence: cut, white, wire, position 2.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤞", "🖐", "🤝", "✌"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Send the manual rule to Deaf as a sequence of legal gestures. Deaf must then say the gesture names and order to me, in addition to the bomb readings.
Deaf says to Mute: Current visual state: display 9, light green, painted strip blue-yellow-blue, keypad 1=2 2=9 3=0 4=8, one digit required, none entered, wires 1 blue 2 white 3 red 4 purple 5 orange 6 green.

The manual remains exactly “Cut the white wire.” Deaf’s visual report confirms that the white wire is wire 2. I’ll use an explicit coded sequence: scissors/cut, white, wire, then position 2.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🖐", "🤝", "✌"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Urgent: I still have no manual rule. Please gesture the exact instruction to Deaf this turn, then have Deaf relay it to me next turn. Do not merely gesture a request; communicate the required key or wire and any conditions.
Deaf says to Mute: Current state: display 6, light blue, strip blue-yellow-blue, keypad 1=2 2=9 3=0 4=8, one digit required, none entered, wires 1 blue 2 white 3 red 4 purple 5 orange 6 green.

The manual gives one unconditional action: cut the white wire. Deaf’s reading identifies that wire as position 2, so I’m sending a fixed sequence for cut, white, wire, and wire 2—not a request for more information.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤞", "🖐", "🤝", "✌"])
```
